channel.title: KeeForge for Mac
channel.description: Direct-download updates for KeeForge for Mac.

item.description:
### New Features
- On iPhone and iPad, insert a verification code through the system AutoFill text menu when an app does not recognize its code field. - KeeForge for Mac can be installed with Homebrew: `brew install --cask keeforge/tap/keeforge` installs the direct-download build, which then updates itself (#254). See [KeeForge/homebrew-tap](https://github.com/KeeForge/homebrew-tap) for the one-time `brew trust` step. - iPhone Duo support: opening the phone switches to the iPad layout, with the list beside the entry, and closing it switches back. The open group, the entry you were viewing, search, selected entries, and an unsaved new or edited entry or group all stay as they were. The same now holds when you resize KeeForge's window on iPad. - The password generator creates passwords up to 128 characters long; before, the length slider stopped at 64 (#272). - A protected custom field, once revealed in the entry editor, edits in a box that wraps and grows over several lines, like other custom fields. Before, it edited on a single line, which made long values such as secure notes hard to change (#284). - Create Key File makes a new key file while you create a database or change its master key, so you no longer need another KeePass app for it. KeeForge saves it where you choose as a KeePass `.keyx` file, which KeePass and KeePassXC also open. Keep a copy somewhere safe: without the key file, the database can't be opened (#273).
### Fixes
- When a save stops because of a character a database cannot hold, the message names the entry or group and the field it is in, so you can find and remove it. Before, it named only the character. - Opening a database written by KeePassXC 4.1 with extension data on an entry or group (browser integration, for example) no longer replaces the entry's or group's modification time with that data's own timestamp, which also affected which side won a sync merge. - Saving keeps the protected values inside parts of a database KeeForge does not edit when there are two or more in one place. Before, they were scrambled and read back empty. - A protected value whose stored text is wrapped across lines no longer garbles every protected value after it. A database whose protected value cannot be decoded at all now reports that instead of opening with wrong values. - Saving no longer deletes a creation, modification, or move time, or a history or maintenance setting, that KeeForge cannot read; it is kept as written. - Saving keeps data another app stored at the top level of a database, beside its settings and groups. Before, KeeForge removed it. - On iPhone and iPad, KeeForge's cover now holds in places where it could slip. The app switcher shows the cover instead of the screen you left. During a screen recording, mirroring, or AirPlay, KeeForge stays covered when Face ID, Control Center, Notification Center, or a system alert appears, after you close Control Center or return to the app, and when the recording started before you opened KeeForge. While the cover is up, taps no longer reach the hidden app and the keyboard closes, so nothing typed shows in the recording. - Password and verification-code pickers show credentials for the exact requested host first, offer related hosts as possible matches when none match, and let you search all credentials, including entries without a URL. Rows show the associated hosts, and search includes additional URLs. - In Mac AutoFill, a request to choose a verification code now opens KeeForge's picker. - In AutoFill, a picker you already dismissed can no longer cancel the next request. - On iPhone and iPad, cancelling the Face ID or Touch ID prompt that opens a database by itself now shows the unlock page, so you can enter the password or try again. Before, KeeForge kept showing the opening screen until you swiped it away (#268). - In AutoFill, a search that matches none of the possible matches no longer leaves an empty "Possible matches" heading. - In the Mac app downloaded from the website, the update window shows the release notes instead of a GitHub page. - In AutoFill, entering the master password for a database whose saved key file can't be read now says that the key file is the problem. Before, AutoFill tried the password without the key file and reported a wrong password or a corrupted file, even when the password was correct (#274). - An XML key file with a non-ASCII character near its start now opens its database. Before, KeeForge could misread it as a plain file and derive the wrong key. - On iPhone and iPad with Touch ID, the Auto-Unlock setting now says Touch ID instead of Face ID. - Clearer messages when a database can't be opened: a damaged header and a database too large to open now say so, instead of "Not a KeePass Database" or a generic decompression error. Key files marked version 2.1 now open, and key files with a version KeePass doesn't define say that the version is unsupported.
### Changes
- Turning on Expires for an entry without an expiry date now proposes today at midnight, as KeePass does, instead of a month from now. Saved without changing the date, the entry shows as expired; the presets still set a date 1, 3, 6, or 12 months ahead (#275). - German and Spanish now address you informally (du, tú) everywhere, matching iOS and macOS; before, they switched between formal and informal. Chinese uses 你 throughout, and several inconsistent terms were corrected across languages. - The Mac app downloaded from the website checks for updates automatically once a day, without first asking. Turn it off in Settings → About → Updates, where you can also check now. - iPhone and iPad have a new look built from standard iOS layouts. A database opens on tiles for All Entries, Verification Codes, Tags, and the Recycle Bin with their counts, above its groups; the tiles replace the view menu, so a database now always opens on this overview. Select Entries, Sync Now, and Database Details move into a More menu; selecting entries works like Notes, with Select All and Done at the top and Move to Group at the bottom, and from iOS 26 Delete joins it there and search and New sit at the bottom of the screen. Entries show their icon, or their initials when they use the default key icon, and entry details list fields as label and value rows, with Lock beside Edit and a banner on expired entries. The entry editor groups its fields into Basics, URL, and Tags, and entry history shows the current version above earlier ones. New also offers Scan QR Code, which adds a verification code to a new or existing entry. Unlocking opens as its own page from the database list, with the database's name and file in the navigation bar and the key file and hardware key together in one card. A wrong password or key file shows what went wrong in a card above the fields, so you can correct it and unlock again; other failures explain what went wrong with their recovery actions. The launch screen and the cover shown while KeeForge is in the background use a rounded icon on the app's plain background, and the cover fades out when you return. While the screen is recorded or shared, the cover says that KeeForge's content is hidden. The database list shows each database as a row with its storage icon, file, and when it last synced or was opened, and the database's name sits level with its buttons at the top of the screen. In Database Details, Share is now Export…; the database list keeps Share. New Database shows its settings as label and value rows with the encryption choices always visible and a password strength meter, and the password generator shows its suggestion centered with a strength rating and Regenerate below it and a sample of each character set. While a database opens, KeeForge shows the steps it is on: syncing with the cloud, decrypting, and opening. The database list and Database Details say in words when changes are waiting to upload ("1 change waiting to upload"), and most explanatory footnotes are gone. AutoFill uses the same look and shows each entry's custom icon, and on iPhone and iPad the website icons KeeForge has already downloaded; when nothing matches the website, it names the site and offers to create a login for it or show all credentials. The Mac app keeps its layout; its New Database and password generator sheets follow the same changes.
